name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention: domain=chapter_19, descriptor=post_action. The '19' is a meaningful chapter ID (chapters 01-30 are domain IDs and must be preserved), not an address residue (function is at 0x20926, unrelated to 19). Name accurately reflects the body: a chapter-19 turn-cycle post-action handler dispatched via data_fd2_chapter_post_action_handler_table[18] @ 0x51B19. Consistent with all 18 sibling handlers in chpost.c.
purpose: Chapter 19 turn-cycle post-action handler: runs the default win/lose check, then adds a turn-gated single-slot lose override (from turn 7 onwards, if key NPC runtime_char[0x40] is dead -> LOSE).
logic_summary: Calls fd2_check_battle_end_condition() (default win/lose evaluation). Then, only if the signed turn counter data_fd2_battle_turn_counter (@0x53BEF) is strictly greater than 6 (turn 7+) AND fd2_check_char_is_dead(0x40) returns non-zero, sets data_fd2_chapter_event_or_battle_end_code (@0x53ECC) = 1 (LOSE / game over). The turn gate means slot 0x40 is unprotected before turn 7 (off-map or invulnerable scripted state). Structurally this is chapter 15's single-slot 0x40 lose check wrapped in chapter 13's strict 'turn > 6' gate. Leading __CHK(8,...) is a Watcom stack-overflow-probe prologue artifact, not a real argument.
